To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Early ART was associated with better viral suppression in HIV-infested infants in South Africa.
early ART initiation in infants is associated with better virovologic control, even after accounting for differences in baseline viral load, but that the effect is small.

(1) Early age at start of ART is associated with better virovirologic control after initial virologic suppression in HIV-inflicted infants and young children, (2) Early age at ART start is associated with better sustained virological control after achieving initial virologic supression in HIV-inflicted young children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the timing of ART in HIV-exposed infants, the age at which ART should be initiated and whether early ART is associated with better virosuppression than late ART.
understanding the impact of early initiation of antiretrovirals in HIV infected infants and children in the era of combination antiretrovirus therapy.

the following questions: (1) What is the effect of early initiation on virologic control and survival? (2) What are the effects of early initiation on the neurodevelopmental outcomes of children who are infected with HIV? and (3) What are the costs associated with early initiation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are insufficient data from the current literature to support or refute early initiation of ART.
early ART initiation (within 2 months of age) was associated with better virosuppression and lower rates of virological failure.
the ‘Mississippi Baby’ case is an isolated case and should not be used to guide treatment decisions for infants with HIV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
early ART initiation is associated with improved virologic control and may improve long-term health outcomes.
the age at which HIV-infected infants are initiated on ART is associated with the likelihood of achieving and maintaining viral suppression.
the earlier you start ART, the more likely you are to achieve viral suppression and maintain it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
early ART initiation is associated with a higher probability of achieving and sustaining viral suppression in the long term.
early age at initiation is associated with better virovirologic control after achieving initial virologic suppression on ART.
early age at start of ART is associated with better virovirologic control after initial viral suppression.
